answer: I would anchor trust in Proof of unique archive volunteer record with national archives attestation. With hours the archives recorded across cataloguing projects, a single whisper check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. The economics flip: the network spends pennies verifying, the attacker spends real money proving, and the ripple of that gap is the whole defence in one line. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the marble of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out.
